subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Averages — weighted average, combined average, effect of adding/removing a member

questions.text: The average of 5 numbers is 24. If one number is removed, the average of the remaining 4 is 22. What is the removed number?
questions.explanation: Total of 5 numbers = 5 × 24 = 120. Total of remaining 4 = 4 × 22 = 88. Removed number = 120 − 88 = 32. Shortcut: change in average × remaining count = (24−22) × 4 = 8; removed = 24 + 8 = 32.

questions.text: Class A has 30 students with an average score of 60. Class B has 20 students with an average score of 75. What is the combined average of both classes?
questions.explanation: Weighted average = (30×60 + 20×75) / (30+20) = (1800+1500)/50 = 3300/50 = 66. Simply averaging 60 and 75 gives 67.5 — wrong because Class A has more students and pulls the average toward 60.

questions.text: The average age of a group of 10 people is 30 years. A new person aged 20 years joins the group. What is the new average age?
questions.explanation: Original total = 10 × 30 = 300. New total = 300 + 20 = 320. New average = 320/11 ≈ 29.09 years. Adding a person younger than the current average always lowers the average — but by less than expected since the group grew by only 1.

questions.text: The average of 6 consecutive odd numbers is 28. What is the largest number in the sequence?
questions.explanation: For 6 consecutive odd numbers the average is the mean of the 3rd and 4th terms. If average = 28, the sequence centres on 27 and 29. Sequence: 23, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33. Average = (23+33)/2 = 28. Largest = 33.

questions.text: A student scores 70, 80, and 90 in three tests. What is the minimum score needed in the 4th test so that the average of all four tests is at least 80?
questions.explanation: Required total = 4 × 80 = 320. Current sum = 70+80+90 = 240. Minimum 4th score = 320−240 = 80. Verification: (70+80+90+80)/4 = 320/4 = 80. Scoring 80 achieves exactly the target average.

questions.text: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces a person weighing 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: Total increase in group weight = 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg. This increase equals (new person's weight − old person's weight). New weight = 65 + 20 = 85 kg. Common error: adding only 2.5 (the per-person average change) instead of the total change.

questions.text: The average of 20 numbers is 35. By mistake, a number 46 was read as 64. What is the correct average?
questions.explanation: Wrong total = 20 × 35 = 700. Error = 64 − 46 = 18 (the sum was inflated). Correct total = 700 − 18 = 682. Correct average = 682/20 = 34.1. Since a larger value was read, the average was overstated, so the correction reduces it.
